transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-21 | Time: 3:00 PM PT | Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Warden Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Warden Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Warden Data Scientist)
Recording ID: ff-2026-06-21-warden-emb-rank-001

Summary (auto): quick discovery about Warden's plan to add semantic search and reranking for their support & KB product. They currently use Elastic for keyword search, evaluating vector pipeline for hybrid search. Main asks: throughput for 5M vectors, dimensionality tradeoffs, hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), and rerank architecture (ANN prefilter + cross-encoder cost). Next steps: pricing, security docs, benchmark plan, pilot.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, uh, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE for your account. With me is Priya our SE, she'll take the deep dive. How's everybody doing?
[00:10] Marta Ruiz: Good, thanks Jordan. Excited to learn more, we've, uh, been kicking the tires on vector search internally.
[00:15] Ethan Cole: Yep hi all, Ethan here. We're the infra folks, so I care about throughput, costs, and VPC options.
[00:20] Priya Singh: And I'm Priya, data scientist, I'll be driving embedding choices and reranker evals.

[00:30] Priya Nair: Great. Quick agenda - we'll ask about your current stack, numbers (QPS, dataset size), then walk through Redwood hosted/dedicated/private options and how embeddings + rerank would look, and finish with next steps. Sound good?
[00:40] Marta: Sounds good.

[01:05] Jordan: Maybe to start Marta, can you give us the background and what success looks like?
[01:15] Marta: Sure. Warden is building a support knowledge product - right now search is Elastic with some BM25 boosting. Users complain about hard matches and synonyms, so we want semantic. Success = precision up for top-3 answers and latency stay below 200ms on average for search. For reranking we're willing to accept a bit higher latency if relevance improves.
[01:40] Priya Singh: To add, we expect peak search QPS about 150-200 qps, average maybe 60. Our corpus is roughly 5 million documents - mix of short FAQs and full KB articles. Storage currently in S3, metadata in Postgres.

[02:05] Ethan: Another constraint - data residency. Some content is EU-only, and we need SOC2 and SSO/SAML for our vendors. Also prefer VPC peering for private deployments.

[02:30] Priya Nair: Great, that's super helpful. Let me run through options quickly: Redwood Hosted (fastest to get started), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput), Redwood Private - VPC/on-prem for strict security. For embeddings + rerank, pattern is usually: generate embeddings (either with Redwood hosted models or bring your own), store in a vector index (managed or self-hosted), do ANN pre-filter then optionally rerank top-K with a cross-encoder.

[03:15] Marta: We were looking at Pinecone and Milvus. How does Redwood play with those?
[03:25] Priya Nair: We integrate with standard vector DBs - Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, and you can also host FAISS indices on Dedicated or Private. For Hosted customers, we have connectors and recommended config. One common pattern is: generate embeddings via Redwood API, stream them into Pinecone, then query Pinecone for nearest neighbors and then send top-100 (or top-50) to a reranker model.
[03:55] Priya Singh: Top-100? That's a lot. We're thinking more like top-20 then rerank with a cross-encoder. Latency becomes a concern.
[04:05] Priya Nair: Totally - top-20 is common. You can tune K. For cross-encoder rerank, latency depends on model size. Typical numbers: ANN lookup <50-100ms for optimized HNSW on dedicated nodes, cross-encoder on CPU can be 200-600ms depending on model; on GPU you can get 50-200ms. So for a strict 200ms end-to-end SLO, you'd likely do ANN + a light reranker or run the reranker on dedicated GPU pool.
[04:45] Ethan: Do you have guidance on embedding dimensionality? Our current model embeddings are 1536-d, we considered down-projection to 768 to save storage/cost.
[04:55] Priya Nair: Good question. Tradeoffs: 1536 dims (e.g., larger transformer embeddings) usually give better recall for subtle semantics, but index size and QPS cost increase. Quick math - 5M vectors * 1536 dims * 4 bytes (float32) ~ 30.7GB raw; plus index overhead can be 2-3x depending on index type and metadata. If you quantize (FP16 or PQ) and use HNSW+PQ, storage drops significantly. Moving to 768 reduces raw bytes by half. But it's model dependent - you should run evals. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and model choices based on a sample workload.
[05:45] Marta: For our team, disk and memory are concerns. We don't want to pay huge RAM costs for HNSW. Can Dedicated help?
[05:55] Priya Nair: Dedicated gives predictable GPU/VM pools and you can colocate vector index (FAISS) on same private cluster or use managed Pinecone but with reserved capacity. We also support hybrid configs where the ANN index is in a vector DB and reranker runs on Redwood Dedicated GPUs. That reduces network hops and latency.
[06:20] Jordan: Quick note - when folks say 'Redwood Dedicated', sometimes we say 'Redwood Dedicate' in notes, so apologies for typos in recordings.

[06:30] Ethan: About throughput - you mentioned 150-200 qps peak. For 200 qps with ANN + rerank, roughly what GPU footprint do we need?
[06:40] Priya Nair: It depends on reranker model. For example, a small cross-encoder (distil-bert-ish) on a single A10G can handle several hundred inferences per second with batching; larger models require more GPUs. A practical approach: run ANN prefilter to reduce candidates to top-20 then run batch rerank. With continuous batching, throughput improves a lot. For strict per-request latency, make sure batching window is small. We can provide a sizing estimate in the benchmark plan.

[07:20] Marta: Do you support hybrid search - BM25 + vector? We want to keep some keyword relevance for legal references.
[07:30] Priya Nair: Yes - hybrid is common. You can do a weighted fusion of BM25 and cosine/sim scores, or use the vector DB's hybrid features. We often recommend prefilter with BM25 to narrow corpus, then ANN over that subset, or score-fuse results. Implementation details depend on vector DB capabilities.

[07:55] Priya Singh: On rerank model choices - are there recommended models from Redwood? Also can we bring our own models?
[08:05] Priya Nair: You can bring your own. Redwood hosts curated models and we have verified performance profiles. For rerank, smaller cross-encoders or specialized rerankers are typical. We also support running your custom PyTorch/ONNX models in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, we have a model catalog and verified latency profiles.

[08:40] Ethan: For security we need KMS integration and audit logs. How granular are audit trails?
[08:50] Jordan: We support KMS/HSM integrations and provide audit logs with request-level traces in Redwood Console. For Private deployments you get customer-controlled KMS and VPC peering. We can share the security whitepaper.

[09:10] Marta: Any gotchas with vector DB consistency or indexing latency when you ingest 5M vectors? We have nightly ingestion jobs.
[09:20] Priya Nair: Ingest patterns matter. For large bulk ingests, indexing can take time depending on index type. Some DBs support background indexing and fast insert, others need reindex. If you use FAISS on Dedicated, you can shard and rebuild incrementally. We'll put recommended strategies in the benchmark plan.

[09:45] Priya Singh: For evaluation, we care about MRR for top-5 and user satisfaction metrics. Can Redwood help with evaluation harnesses?
[09:55] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes eval tooling that runs A/B tests, tracks quality regressions against prompt sets, and alerts on drift. We can help set up MRR and hit rates for your test queries.

[10:20] Ethan: Licensing question - if we go Dedicated vs Private, what's the contract model?
[10:30] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based. Dedicated is reserved capacity contracts monthly or annually with committed throughput and a lower per-token/unit price. Private is enterprise license plus support. We'll include options in the pricing doc.

[10:50] Marta: What's the typical pilot sizing? We've budgeted for a 2-week pilot ingesting a subset.
[11:00] Priya Nair: Pilots are usually 1-2 weeks, ingest sample of corpus or the full 5M depending on goals. For rerank benching, ingest 5M vectors and run a bench that measures recall, MRR, and end-to-end latency. We'll provide a config that uses HNSW + PQ and a small cross-encoder for rerank.

[11:35] Jordan: Anything else from Warden?
[11:40] Marta: Just timeline - we hope to decide by end of Q3, so pilots in July would be ideal.
[11:50] Ethan: I'll send our dataset schema and expected QPS.
[11:55] Priya Singh: I'll share a small labeled eval set of 2k queries.

[12:05] Priya Nair: Great. Recap of next steps: we'll send hosted vs dedicated pricing, security docs, and a benchmark plan. We'll schedule the technical deep dive next week to finalize pilot details.

[12:25] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the pack.

[12:30] Meeting end.
